```{=html}
<!-- The payoff slide's figure ("Same format. No drift."). Two CSVs feed ONE
     .qmd, and two PDFs fall out of it. This is the previous slide's
     parameterization drawn instead of described: the content has an address,
     the address is an argument, and the format never enters the conversation.

     The slide's two sheet images and its .notes stay in index.qmd; only the
     drawing lives here, pulled in with {{< include svg/params.qmd >}}.

     INVARIANTS
     - No ids, no <defs>, no markers. Arrowheads are explicit triangles (15 wide,
       17.5 long, base overlapped 3 units by its line), so this figure adds
       nothing to the document-wide id namespace. Keep it that way.
     - The .qmd box is the entanglement figure's box at its own scale: 190x124,
       rx=6, white fill, navy 2.5 stroke, teal yaml band 158x36. The yaml band is
       what does not vary, and it is the only thing on the slide that is drawn
       once instead of twice. Do not recolor it, do not move it.
     - The content block is an empty SLOT -- white, dashed navy, labelled
       `content`. It is not yellow and not red on purpose: the colors live on the
       CSV boxes now, so the slot reads as the thing either file can occupy.
       Filling it picks a winner and kills the parameterization claim.
     - pokemon wears the at-rest content yellow #edae49 with navy text; minecraft
       wears the post-click red #d1495b with white text. That pairing is
       entanglement figure 2's click, frozen -- read left to right it is the
       animation. Text on yellow is navy, text on red is white; legibility, not
       taste.
     - Arrows are navy ink, never colored to match their CSV. Yellow is invisible
       as a line (1.6:1) and a red-only link would say the two sides differ in
       kind. Left/right position carries the pairing instead: pokemon top-left
       and bottom-left, minecraft top-right and bottom-right.
     - The two output arrows leave the .qmd box at its thirds (x=438 and x=502),
       not from one shared stem at the centre. Two departures say two renders;
       a single stem that splits would say one render produced both sheets, which
       is the one thing this figure must not claim.
     - Fan endpoints (x=240, x=700) are the quarter and three-quarter points of
       the viewBox, so they land roughly over the two images below. Roughly is
       the requirement; exact registration would depend on the rendered width and
       is not worth chasing.
     - The two output arrows are cubic beziers with VERTICAL tangents at both
       ends, the same idiom as the experiment figure's fan, so the drawn triangle
       (which cannot rotate) still points straight down into the sheet. The
       control points sit 46 units past each endpoint (y=200 and y=150), not at
       the midpoint: the drop is only 42 units against ~200 of horizontal travel,
       and pulling the controls in whips the curve into a kink right where the
       arrowhead is. If either endpoint moves, re-check that overhang. -->
<svg viewBox="10 2 920 218" width="1120" height="266"
     xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     font-family="'Fira Sans Condensed', Tahoma, sans-serif">

  <!-- the .qmd -->
  <text x="470" y="20" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle"
        fill="#2e4057" font-family="SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace">.qmd</text>
  <rect x="375" y="30" width="190" height="124" rx="6"
        fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <rect x="391" y="46" width="158" height="36" fill="#00798c"/>
  <text x="470" y="71" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle"
        fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace">yaml</text>
  <rect x="391" y="94" width="158" height="44"
        fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 5"/>
  <text x="470" y="123" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle"
        fill="#2e4057" font-family="SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace">content</text>

  <!-- pokemon.csv, left, pointing in -->
  <rect x="27" y="88" width="260" height="56" fill="#edae49"/>
  <text x="157" y="123" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle"
        fill="#2e4057" font-family="SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace">pokemon.csv</text>
  <path d="M 295 116 L 357 116" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <path d="M 354 108.5 L 371.5 116 L 354 123.5 z" fill="#2e4057"/>

  <!-- minecraft.csv, right, pointing in -->
  <rect x="653" y="88" width="260" height="56" fill="#d1495b"/>
  <text x="783" y="123" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle"
        fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace">minecraft.csv</text>
  <path d="M 645 116 L 583 116" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <path d="M 586 108.5 L 568.5 116 L 586 123.5 z" fill="#2e4057"/>

  <!-- two renders, leaving the box at its thirds, out to the two sheets below -->
  <path d="M 438 154 C 438 200, 240 150, 240 196"
        stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5" fill="none"/>
  <path d="M 232.5 193 L 240 210.5 L 247.5 193 z" fill="#2e4057"/>
  <path d="M 502 154 C 502 200, 700 150, 700 196"
        stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5" fill="none"/>
  <path d="M 692.5 193 L 700 210.5 L 707.5 193 z" fill="#2e4057"/>
</svg>
```
